reviewed_by: cold-start test (practice), not a person's review, 2026-11-01
notes: Practice piece (cold-start test 2, 1 November 2026). Test questions T1-T4 from runs/cold-2-research.md section 7, worded exactly as asked, so mark_run.py can match them by question text.
Chat plan: T1, T2 and T4 are fresh chats. T2 is a Repeat of T1 (same wording, family best_month; its rivals are T1's rows). T3 is a Follow-up of T1, asked in T1's chat.

'Month' is the calendar month of order_purchase_timestamp, read from the raw string's first seven characters (YYYY-MM), no timezone conversion, as the metrics note says. 'Best' has no stated metric: the primary reading is delivered merchandise revenue (SUM(price), delivered orders), the metrics note's default revenue. Rivals: delivered order count, all-status order count, all-status merchandise revenue, delivered revenue including freight.

Every row computes the value in the best month under its reading (the maximum monthly value), because mark_run.py marks one number. Which month an answer names is not marked by mark_run.py; rows T1m and T4m (asked: false, no family) give the best month as a number YYYYMM under the primary reading, for a person to compare with the month the answer names.

T3's primary reading carries T1's delivered scope: the most delivered orders in any purchase month. Rivals: the most orders of any status in a month; and the reading 'how many orders did [T1's] best month have', i.e. delivered (T3c) or all-status (T3d) order count in the month with the highest delivered revenue.
T4 restricts every T1 reading to purchase timestamps in 2017.
The last months of the data (September and October 2018) are thin; a 'best month' over the full data is not affected by them, so no row excludes them. reviewed_by is left for a person.
